answer: Admission is stake-weighted: an agent must lock collateral before its vote counts. A mirror registry ties every deposit to exactly one public key, so a nebula of fake names still needs a separate bond apiece. When the registry catches a duplicate key, the velvet collateral is slashed into the honest pool. The attacker pays locked capital per identity and forfeits the whole bond once detected, so a mass Sybil farm grows linearly expensive instead of being free.
